Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as ada6baa945fbd1bd1969facb1d7dc2fc12453f2e
Is it possible to put this buffer on the stack?
we could easily reset and free up this with dynamic allocation or in future create other buffers required which may point to the same requestBuffer if needed.
Can we directly have interface object of type `std::shared_ptr<sdbusplus::asio::dbus_interface>` as parameter instead?
Acknowledged
Can we add `Name` or `Path` of the Inventory object as well in the log?
yes Name is sufficient.
Can we add `Name` or `Path` of the Inventory object as well in the log?
Acknowledged
Can this be private?
yes but it will help us later if we have use case to trigger any single property refresh from outside.
nit: dont need this
Acknowledged
Can you do this even without checking DeviceType?

Currently I have kept this as common code for all device types. The only thing that has device type check is the type of device itself. When we add more device type we can put any other conditions required.
Why would we add accelerator to CX?
Ok I see. Fixed it.
string_view is better
the register_property requires the same signature.

Would it be better to implement the property update book keeping and retry mechanism outside of this? I see that class of `Memory` also uses similar logic. This common logic can be used there directly?

I had tried that initially but it becomes so complex because of the differences in encode/decode APIs and buffer used for that. The framework in inventory uses single buffer and does sequential processing of properties. This might not be applicable for all other properties. If we have abstract all of this then at the common code its has not much to make it generic.
Do we need a log for the else case?
Acknowledged
I think we should retry based on rc/cc?
success flag here is set based on rc/cc.
Let's avoid a double find()
Acknowledged
It is possible we can start off sensor reads while we're waiting here, right? Any concerns doing that?
no there is no concern. If its for same EID then request would be queued.
Is this (and the other functions in this call stack) used in this commit? If not, please remove.

update API can be used at later point if for some invent handling we want to refresh all the properties. Currently only Inventory object creation does property fetch which can fail after 3 retires. At later point in time if we want to refresh the properties then we can use the update API.
Let's not add dead code in this commit.
Acknowledged

Is it better to call this function in constructor itself based on the type of the device? If we are going to use only one class for all device type we might have to fetch only selected properties based on device type.

update can help us for any future implementation where we might have to refresh inventory property after invent like re-discovery. We can add any device type logic in future if its applicable. for now its all common.
Do all these need to be public?
Acknowledged
Do we really need the name here?
yes propertyName used as a key to update the interface. We could have more than one property on the interface.
Based on the name, hard to distinghuish what this one vs requestInventoryProperty does
Acknowledged
Still not clear to me 😊. The other one makes a request. This one?

fetchInventoryProperty - API which checks if any inventory property is pending to be updated. It runs through the map and find what needs to be updated. I have renamed this one now for more clarity. 

sendInventoryPropertyRequest takes property ID does encode and makes the actual request.
This one is marked const but the others are not. Are both intentional?
yes because others change the member variables.
